name: Lin Bu
credit: Kitayama Kangan, portrait of Lin Bu (Japanese, late 18th century) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Lin Bu (林逋; 967–1028) was a Northern Song poet who lived as a recluse at West Lake near Hangzhou, refusing office and, it is said, never marrying. Tradition has it that he "took the plum as his wife and the crane as his son", planting plum trees on his hillside and keeping cranes.

He is remembered above all for his plum-blossom poems, whose couplet on sparse shadows and hidden fragrance became a model for later poets and painters. He is also known by the posthumous title Hejing.

poems.title: 山園小梅 其一 (Shan yuan xiao mei, qi yi)
poems.author: Lin Bu
poems.collection: 千家詩 (Poems of a Thousand Poets)
poems.text:
衆芳搖落獨鮮妍，占斷風情向小園。
疏影橫斜水清淺，暗香浮動月黃昏。
霜禽欲下先偷眼，粉蝶如知合斷魂。
幸有微吟可相狎，不須檀板共金樽。
